question: Does the source's overall-average household-size conversion describe the members of the wealth-ranked bottom38%? Inspect weighted actual household/primary-economic-unit sizes in current public2016 files, without assuming these are the exact2020-vintage files or proving individual ownership.
stage: primary-data feasibility audit, not candidate/confirmation/final evaluation

targets: Full public2016 Stata main dataset (approximately10MB ZIP)

analysis_predeclaration: Inspect identifiers and documented fields before computing; do not guess an unavailable field. Join full main data's Y1,YY1,X101 (household members),X7001 (primary economic unit members),X42001 (weight) to summary Y1,YY1,WGT,NETWORTH.

The current official macro defines WGT=X42001/5. Verify that relationship and all one-to-one joins; stop on mismatch instead of silently rescaling. Derive implicate as Y1-10*YY1 per the official codebook and require five implicates.

Report pooled WGT-weighted estimates and five per-implicate estimates using full weights (WGT*5). Sort by NETWORTH and take the bottom37% and38% by weighted household mass, using a fractional boundary record; report boundary mass explicitly.

For both cutoffs report weighted household mass, actual X101/X7001 member mass, aggregate wealth in the extract's declared current units, and the 2.63-times-household proxy. Record whether actual member mass reaches125 million, without inferring individual asset ownership.

Do not call five implicates independent seeds or confidence bounds. No sampling-variance claim without replicate weights, which are outside this audit. No direct comparison to nominal2020 Forbes dollars without a verified inflation/version mapping.

An estimate is a current-version diagnostic, not a reproduction of Bruenig/Gross. It does not qualify a workflow, clear a gap, or release the conditional68 attempts. Every uncertainty about source vintage, membership scope and individual wealth remains explicit.
controls_before_analysis: Fractional weighted cutoff gives expected household and member totals on a hand-calculated fixture.
Five replicated implicates with weights/5 do not inflate population totals by5.
Bottom37% negative value cannot transfer to bottom38%; membership and money are distinct dimensions.
resource_limits: One worker, two numerical threads,300 seconds/job; existing Python environments only. No service credit use or billing changes.
